We have three different dart games you can choose from. Which rules do you want to see?
In this game, the numbers you hit are added to your score. The player with the highest score at the end of the game wins. In Count-Up, both the bull's-eye and double bull's-eye are worth 50 points.

In this game, the points you hit are deducted from the designated score as you try to reach exactly zero. There are a variety of starting scores, such as 301 and 501. In '01, both the bull's-eye and double bull's-eye are worth 50 points.
You bust if you go under zero, at which point your opponent gets to play. Your points will revert to what they were when the round started.

The first player to reach exactly zero at the end of the assigned number of rounds wins. If neither player can reach zero during the allotted rounds, the player with fewer remaining points is declared the winner.
In Cricket, only the numbers 15 through 20 and the bull's-eye are used. Singles count as one hit, Doubles count as two hits, and Triples count as three hits.
Three hits on a number closes it. The points from subsequent hits on a number you closed are added to your score.
However, if your opponent closes that number as well, you will no longer get points when you hit it.

When all rounds are concluded, the player with the highest score at the end of the assigned number of rounds wins. You can also win if you close all the numbers before the end of the assigned number of rounds and your score is higher than your opponent's.
Another rule in Cricket states that when there's at least a 200-point difference in the scores, the winning player stops earning points. This is known as overkill.
The player in overkill cannot score hit counts or points on open numbers with one exception: hit counts that do not involve points are valid as usual.

Example: You are winning by 200 points and your first throw hits 15, your second throw also hits 15, and your third throw hits double 15. The hit count of the third throw is limited to one, resulting in a total hit count of three for the round.

Note that if the score gap is 199 or less, points exceeding 200 are awarded, and the hit count is also valid. Example: You are winning by 199 points, and you hit triple 20: Your hit count is three, and you get 60 points, raising your point total to 259.
